data.name: DriverRating.HowDuels
data.value: Each race is a series of duels with the drivers of your class: finishing ahead of a driver is a win against them. Beating a higher-rated driver earns more, losing to a lower-rated driver costs more.

data.name: DriverRating.HowFormula
data.value: Before the race, the ratings forecast a place for everyone (“expected”): 1, plus the chance of each opponent to finish ahead of you. After the race: change = K × (expected place − actual place) ÷ number of opponents, with K = 32 (64 during calibration). Example: 4th of 20 for an expected place of 8.8 gives 32 × 4.8 ÷ 19 = +8.

data.name: DriverRating.HowBounds
data.value: A race therefore moves the rating by less than 32 points (64 during calibration), whatever the size of the grid. The winner always gains points, the last always loses some.

data.name: DriverRating.HowRacesOnly
data.value: Only races count, class by class, on the official class position: retirements, disqualifications and cars still on track when the file was saved included. A class without any finisher is not rated: when you leave a race, LMU saves the other drivers still on track, without a result.

data.name: DriverRating.HowMerges
data.value: Driver merges from Settings are taken into account. The rating only measures the grids of your result files: it is not LMU’s official ranking.
